## Problem

The Agent Register exists as a mature governance spreadsheet (v0.3 — 62 columns, 21 sheets, 19 agents) with a well-defined data model, governance controls, and a lifecycle diagram. A Canvas PowerApp has been built to v12 with working navigation, tabs, linked actions, and SharePoint Lists as the data layer. However there is no single authoritative analysis that:

1. Maps the full xlsx field set to the current Lists/app schema and surfaces gaps.
2. Defines the current data schema in machine-readable form for developers.
3. Specifies the future schema required when the ADO pivot lands (Phase 2 mesh).
4. Produces architecture and sequence diagrams that devs and stakeholders can share.
5. Gives a structured UI/UX critique of what the app must do differently to serve users who are accustomed to the richness of the spreadsheet.
6. Lists specific recommendations with enough context to act on immediately.
7. Surfaces questions that Dom needs answered before the next build sprint.

The gap between "spreadsheet governance artefact" and "working Canvas app" is not yet bridged analytically.

## Vision

Dom opens this analysis, reads the data schemas once, and immediately knows what every field is, where it lives, and how the ADO pivot changes the picture. He pastes the architecture diagram into the next steering deck. He sends the UX critique to the developer team and it provokes immediate action on three or four specific screens. He takes the recommendations list into the next sprint planning session and uses it to sequence the next six weeks of work. The questions section gives him a precise agenda for the next governance review. Euphoric surprise comes when the schema design surfaces a structural flaw that nobody had named yet — the analysis earns its cost by being the thing that prevents a rebuild in three months.

## Out of Scope

This is a read-and-analyse task. No code is written, no app screens are modified, no SharePoint lists are provisioned, no ADO integration is implemented. The ADO Phase 2 write-back design is out of scope — only the schema fields needed for Phase 1 (read-only sync) are specified. Dataverse migration design is noted but not detailed. Power Automate flow design is not covered. The analysis does not cover authentication/RBAC design within the app. No new mockups are produced — the existing v1 build pack mockups are used as the UX reference.

## Principles

1. **Schema must reflect governance reality.** Fields exist because governance requires them — not because they are technically convenient. Field design must preserve the mandatory/optional distinction from the xlsx `*` notation.
2. **Separation of concerns is non-negotiable.** ADO owns delivery execution; the Power App owns governance. Any field that lives in both must have a clear owner and a stated sync direction.
3. **Child lists over wide tables.** Repeatable rows (knowledge sources, test questions, readiness checks) belong in child lists. The parent Agents list must remain queryable and filterable without SharePoint delegation issues.
4. **User-facing screens optimise for cognitive load.** Canvas is a constrained rendering environment. Every screen decision should reduce the number of things the user must hold in their head.
5. **The xlsx is the truth, not the enemy.** The spreadsheet captures 62 columns of governance reality. The app must respect that richness — it cannot be a simplified subset without explicit out-of-scope declarations.
6. **ADO pivot must not require a rebuild.** Schema decisions now must leave room for Phase 2 ADO fields without refactoring existing lists.

## Constraints

- Canvas PowerApp is the mandated front-end — no Dataverse-native forms, no model-driven app.
- Microsoft Lists (SharePoint) is the data layer for v1 — Dataverse is a future option only.
- SharePoint List column limits: practical threshold ~300 columns before performance degrades; single list must stay well under this.
- Azure DevOps integration is Phase 1 read-only — no write-back in the current build sprint.
- Canvas lacks a native kanban component — Pipeline board requires a custom horizontal gallery pattern.
- Agent name max length: 42 characters (xlsx constraint, enforced by the template).
- The app must work within a single Power Platform environment (Default-e476cf3e...).

Produce a complete analytical reference for the Agent Register app covering: (1) the current data schema mapped from xlsx v3 to Lists, (2) the future schema post-ADO pivot, (3) an architecture diagram, (4) a sequence flow diagram, (5) a structured UI/UX critique, (6) a prioritised recommendations list, and (7) a questions agenda — sufficient that a developer team can act without further archaeology.

# 61 — Agent Register v3 Analysis

**Date:** 2026-06-10  
**Source:** xlsx v3 vs repo comparison (v61 build)  
**Scope:** Current data schema, future ADO pivot schema, architecture, sequence flow, UI/UX review, recommendations, questions

---

## Diagrams

- Architecture: `docs/diagrams/README.md` (Excalidraw checkpoint `b6b96ea5b9c84185bc`)
- Sequence Flow: `docs/diagrams/README.md` (Excalidraw checkpoint `74312e0d6d3843b39a`)
- Obsidian: `03 Spaces/Work/Excalidraw/Agent Register Architecture 2026-06-10.excalidraw.md`
- Obsidian: `03 Spaces/Work/Excalidraw/Agent Register Lifecycle Sequence 2026-06-10.excalidraw.md`

---

## Current Data Schema: xlsx → SharePoint Lists

### Core: Agents List (62 columns → 40 fields)

| Field Group | xlsx Columns | SP Field | Type | Mandatory |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Identity | Agent Name, Summary, URL | AgentName, AgentSummary, AgentUrl | Single line / Multi-line | Yes |
| Ownership | Owner, Department, Portfolio | Owner, Department, Portfolio | Person / Choice / Lookup | Yes |
| Lifecycle | Stage, ADO State | LifecycleStage, ADODeliveryState | Choice | Yes |
| User Story | As a / I want to / So that | UserStoryAsA, UserWantTo, SoThat | Multi-line | Yes |
| Business case | Problem solved, Target audience | BusinessProblem, TargetAudience | Multi-line | Yes |
| Instructions | Agent instructions | AgentInstructions | Multi-line | Yes |
| Topic titles | Topic titles | AgentTopics | Multi-line | No |
| Risk flags | PII, Web search, Tools, Triggers | ContainsPII, WebSearchEnabled, UsesTools, UsesTriggers | Yes/No | Yes |
| PII notes | PII notes | PIINotes | Multi-line | Conditional |
| Model | Model used | ModelUsed | Choice | No |
| Evaluation | Evaluator, Date, Outcome, Notes, Score | EvaluatorName, EvaluationDate, EvaluationOutcome, EvaluationNotes, FeasibilityScore | Person / Date / Choice / Multi-line / Number | No |
| AIS | AIS reviewer, date, outcome, notes | AISReviewer, AISReviewDate, AISOutcome, AISNotes | Person / Date / Choice / Multi-line | No |
| DoR gate | Status, date, approver | DORStatus, DORDate, DORApprover | Choice / Date / Person | No |
| DoD gate | Status, date, approver | DODStatus, DODDate, DODApprover | Choice / Date / Person | No |
| Prod gate | Status, date, approver | ProdReadyStatus, ProdReadyDate, ProdReadyApprover | Choice / Date / Person | No |
| Deployment | Dev/UAT/Prod URLs, Solution, Dates | StudioUrlDev, StudioUrlUAT, StudioUrlProd, SolutionName, DateFirstDeployed, DateLastReviewed | Hyperlink / Single line / Date | No |
| Completeness | Completion % | TemplateCompletionPct | Number (calculated → stored) | Auto |

### Child Lists (7 — linked via Lookup to Agents)

| List | Key Columns | Rows per agent |
|---|---|---|
| KnowledgeSources | SourceName, Type, URL, Quality, Sensitivity, LoginRequired, AgentAccess, UserAccess | 1–10 |
| TestQuestions | Question, ExpectedBehaviour, PassFail, TestedBy, TestDate | 5–20 |
| ReadinessChecks | CheckItem, Category (DoR/DoD/Prod), Status, EvidenceUrl, Notes | 15–30 |
| Actions | ActionTitle, ActionType, ActionUrl, Description | 1–10 |
| PromotionDecisions | Stage, Decision, DecidedBy, DecisionDate, Notes | 1 per gate |
| Reviews | ReviewType, Reviewer, Date, Outcome, Notes | 1–5 |
| ADOLinks | ADOWorkItemId, WorkItemType, Title, State, URL | 1–5 |

### Reference Lists (5 — controlled vocabularies)

| List | Values |
|---|---|
| Portfolios | Shared Reg, LCAD, … |
| RiskCategories | PII, External data, Tool use, … |
| LifecycleStages | Intake, Evaluate, Approve, Design, Build&QA, UAT, ELS, Live, Retired |
| Environments | Dev, UAT, Prod |
| Personas | Staff, Manager, Citizen, External |

---

## Future Schema: ADO Pivot (Phase 1 — Read-only Sync)

13 new fields added to **Agents List** (Power Automate writes; users read-only):

| Field | Type | Source |
|---|---|---|
| ADOWorkItemId | Number | ADO Agent work item ID |
| ADOWorkItemUrl | Hyperlink | Direct link to ADO item |
| ADODeliveryState | Choice | Agent WIT state |
| ADOIterationPath | Single line | Sprint/iteration |
| ADOAreaPath | Single line | Team area |
| ADOAssignedTo | Single line | ADO assigned engineer |
| ADOLastSyncedAt | Date/Time | When PA last updated |
| ADOBuildBranch | Single line | Linked repo branch |
| ADOSolutionExportUrl | Hyperlink | Solution export artifact |
| ADOEnvironmentsDeploy | Multi-line | Dev/UAT/Prod deploy status JSON |
| ADOReleasePipelineUrl | Hyperlink | Release pipeline link |
| ADOOpenBugCount | Number | Open bugs in ADO |
| ADOLastReleaseDate | Date/Time | Most recent release |

**Phase 2 (write-back — future):** ADOCreateWorkItem (Yes/No), ADOPromotionTrigger (Text), ADOSyncErrors (Multi-line).

---

## UI/UX Review

### Critical Issues

**C1 — Gallery delegation breaks at scale**
`Filter(AgentsList, LifecycleStage.Value = selectedStage)` is not delegable on Choice fields. Works at 19 agents; silently caps at 500 (default delegation limit) at scale with no warning.
*Fix:* Pre-load into collection at OnStart — `ClearCollect(colAgents, AgentsList)`. Filter the collection.

**C2 — Gate enforcement is advisory only**
DoR, DoD, and Production Readiness gates are UI affordances but no enforced constraint exists. Users can set `LifecycleStage = "UAT"` without any gate approval on record. All 19 current agents show `GovernanceApprovalDecision = "Not assessed"` — gates have never been exercised.
*Fix:* Gate transition buttons are the only promotion path. Disable direct LifecycleStage field on form. Gate approval records must exist and be "Approved" before the button activates.

**C3 — PrivateBetaTesters is free-text**
UAT tester list is a comma-delimited string. Cannot query individual testers, send targeted notifications, or track per-tester completion.
*Fix:* Move to UATTesters child list with a Person column, or add a `TestedBy` column to TestQuestions.

**C4 — Kanban board has no native Canvas equivalent**
The Kanban mockup requires drag-and-drop across columns — Canvas has no native Kanban component. Horizontal scroll at tablet viewport is brittle.
*Fix:* Use a Gallery-per-stage layout (fixed columns, no drag). Defer true drag-and-drop to a future model-driven layer.

**C5 — Template completion % is always derived, never stored**
If completeness logic changes, historical snapshots become inconsistent. Formula is fragile at 62 fields with conditional mandatory rules.
*Fix:* Calculate and write `TemplateCompletionPct` to the list on each save via Patch().

**C6 — No breadcrumb or deep-link navigation**
Back returns to register but loses applied filter. No direct URL to a specific agent record in Canvas.
*Fix:* Persist filter state in global variables (`gvSelectedStage`, `gvSelectedPortfolio`). Restore on Back. Use `Param()` with embedded app URL for deep links.

**C7 — No offline or partial-save error handling**
Multi-list Patch on large template saves can fail partially with no user feedback.
*Fix:* Wrap multi-list Patch in `IfError()` with rollback notification. Add connectivity banner.

### Positive Findings

- Tab-based detail navigation (Summary / Gate Review / Knowledge / Delivery / Actions) mirrors natural workflow and avoids information overload.
- Lifecycle stepper gives executives instant visual orientation — high value.
- 5-step intake wizard is a genuine UX win; staged disclosure prevents form abandonment.
- Template completeness indicator (78%) gives developers a clear progress signal.
- Stage badges and color-coded lifecycle bar are polished for a Canvas app.

---

## Recommendations

| ID | Recommendation | Priority | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Enforce gate transitions — gate buttons are the only promotion path; disable direct LifecycleStage field | High | M |
| R2 | Pre-load Agents into collection (ClearCollect on OnStart) — fixes delegation everywhere | High | S |
| R3 | Store TemplateCompletionPct on Patch — write, don't derive on every screen | High | S |
| R4 | Replace PrivateBetaTesters free-text with UATTesters child list | High | M |
| R5 | Replace Kanban drag-drop mockup with Gallery-per-stage board | Medium | M |
| R6 | Persist filter state across navigation + Back-button state restoration | Medium | S |
| R7 | Build Power Automate Phase 1 ADO sync — read-only delivery state closes biggest visibility gap | Medium | L |
| R8 | Add governance health widget — count agents with no gate approvals, flag as governance debt | Medium | M |
| R9 | Wrap all multi-list Patch operations in IfError — silent partial saves are worse than visible errors | Low | S |

---

## Questions

| ID | Question | For |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Gate approvals are not currently enforced — is this intentional or needed before pilot? | Product Owner |
| Q2 | Are the 19 existing agents expected to go back through governance, or is enforcement for new agents only? | Programme Lead |
| Q3 | What is the trigger to start Phase 1 ADO sync build — gated on PowerApp reaching stable state? | Dev Lead |
| Q4 | Who owns the AIS review process and what evidence is required before sign-off? | Compliance / AIS team |
| Q5 | ELS periods are defined but there is no ELS-end automation — is manual promotion to Live acceptable? | Operations |
| Q6 | How many agents are expected in 12 months? This directly determines the delegation risk in R2. | Product Owner |
| Q7 | Is the Kanban board a must-have for v1 or a nice-to-have? It is the hardest screen to build correctly in Canvas. | Stakeholders |
| Q8 | Who validates Knowledge Source sensitivity and LoginRequired flags before UAT — is that part of AIS review? | AIS Reviewer |
| Q9 | Is `Submitted By` always the same as `Owner`? Does the app need to show submitter lineage separately? | UX / Data |

---

## Structural Issues

1. **62-column flat sheet is not a data model.** The 7 child-data groups are repeating-row data masquerading as columns. Normalisation into child lists is non-optional.

2. **Governance state and delivery state are conflated.** `LifecycleStage` tracks both build progress and production maturity (Introduction/Growth/Maturity/Decline). These need two separate indicators: **Delivery Stage** (Intake→Live) and **Adoption Maturity** (New→Decline).

3. **No single source of truth for stage.** Stage currently exists in both PowerApp and ADO. Without Phase 1 sync, they will diverge. PowerApp is SoT until ADO sync; after Phase 1, ADO delivery state becomes primary signal for build progress.

4. **Silent governance debt.** All 19 agents show `GovernanceApprovalDecision = "Not assessed"` with no flag visible on dashboard. An executive sees no signal that none of these agents have been formally approved. Highest governance risk.

5. **Evidence fields are free text.** AIS review outcome, gate approvals, and production readiness sign-offs are text strings with no attachment, link, or audit trail enforced. Not defensible in a compliance audit.

---

## Overall Assessment

**Maturity: 6.5/10.** Strong visual design, clear workflow metaphor, solid SharePoint schema foundation. The ISC gap is governance enforcement — the bones are right but the gates are decorative. R1 + R2 + R3 + R4 in two sprints would close the most critical defects and make it defensible for pilot. ADO sync (R7) is the highest-leverage Phase 2 feature.

**Single priority decision:** Before the next build sprint, decide whether gate enforcement (R1) is in scope. Everything else is improvement; that one is correctness.

name: obsidian-excalidraw-format
description: Correct format for Obsidian Excalidraw files — use parsed + Drawing json block, validate before writing
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Never use `excalidraw-plugin: raw`. Always use `excalidraw-plugin: parsed` with the standard markdown structure.

**Why:** `raw` mode caused a JSON parse error ("no minus sign at json position") because Obsidian's plugin tried to parse the frontmatter as part of the JSON body. All existing vault files use `parsed`.

**How to apply:** Every `.excalidraw.md` file written to Obsidian must follow this exact structure:

```
---
title: <name>.excalidraw
type: note
date: YYYY-MM-DD
tags: [excalidraw]
excalidraw-plugin: parsed
---
==⚠  Switch to EXCALIDRAW VIEW in the MORE OPTIONS menu of this document. ⚠==

%%
## Drawing
```json
{...excalidraw JSON...}
```
%%
```

Additional rules:
- Use `json.dumps(scene, ensure_ascii=False)` — never default ascii escapes (`—` breaks some parsers)
- All coordinates must be integers, not floats (`121` not `121.0`)
- Always validate JSON with `python3 -c "import json; json.loads(content)"` before writing
- Test render by checking file structure: frontmatter → warning line → `%%` → `## Drawing` → ` ```json ` → JSON → ` ``` ` → `%%`
- Filter out `cameraUpdate` pseudo-elements before writing to file (not valid Excalidraw scene elements)
- Convert MCP `label` shorthand to proper `boundElements` + separate `text` elements with `containerId`

# Memory Index

- [Obsidian Excalidraw format](feedback_obsidian_excalidraw_format.md) — Use `parsed` + `## Drawing json` block; validate JSON before writing; never use `raw` mode

# 62 — RBAC, Audit Log & ADO Sync Specification

**Date:** 2026-06-10  
**Status:** Codex handover — implementation ready  
**Version target:** v62 (next build after v61)  
**Derives from:** Q&A answers in session 2026-06-10; doc 61 analysis

---

## 1. Summary of Changes Driving This Spec

| Question | Answer | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| Gate enforcement before pilot? | Not needed | R1 moves to post-pilot backlog |
| Existing agents back through governance? | Some, not all | Add `GovernanceReviewRequired` flag; admin sets manually |
| ADO sync trigger? | Can start now, parallel workstream | Spec Phase 1 sync flow below |
| AIS review ownership + RBAC? | Multiple roles, needs RBAC + audit log | New `Agent Roles` list; extend `Change Log`; role-gated controls throughout |
| ELS→Live promotion? | Pipeline already exists in ADO | PowerApp reflects state, doesn't drive it; ADO sync surfaces this |
| Agents in 12 months? | ~100 | R2 (collection pre-load) remains correct; child list collections filtered on detail screen |
| Kanban for v1? | Nice-to-have only | Drop from v1 scope |
| Knowledge source sensitivity validator? | Role-based (AIS Reviewer) | Covered by RBAC spec |
| Submitted By = Owner? | No | Add `Submitted By` as separate Person field |

---

## 2. Schema Changes

### 2.1 New List: `Agent Roles`

This list is the single source of truth for who has which role in the PowerApp. It is managed by Admins only (SharePoint list permissions: Admins = Full Control; everyone else = Read).

| Column | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Title` | Single line | Yes | Display name (e.g. "Jane Smith — AIS Reviewer") |
| `UserEmail` | Single line (indexed) | Yes | Lowercase email. Used as lookup key. |
| `DisplayName` | Single line | Yes | Full name for display |
| `Role` | Choice | Yes | See role values below |
| `IsActive` | Yes/No | Yes | Default: Yes. Set No to revoke without deleting |
| `Notes` | Multi-line | No | Reason for assignment, review date |

**Role choice values (closed list — do not add without updating permission matrix):**

| Role | Who it covers |
|---|---|
| `Admin` | App owners, platform engineers. Full access. Manages Agent Roles list. |
| `Evaluator` | Idea evaluators, feasibility reviewers. Can set evaluation outcome and notes. |
| `AIS_Reviewer` | AI CoE assurance team. Can set AIS review fields and validate knowledge sensitivity. |
| `GateApprover` | Senior leads, service owners. Can approve DoR, DoD and Production Readiness gates. |
| `Developer` | Agent builders. Can edit template, knowledge sources, test questions, build fields. |
| `ReadOnly` | Default for anyone not in the list. View all, edit nothing. |

> One user can only have one role. If a person needs Evaluator + GateApprover access, give them GateApprover (wider permissions). If edge cases appear, revisit the role model rather than adding multi-role complexity now.

---

### 2.2 Extend Existing List: `Change Log`

The existing `Change Log` list is extended to serve as the audit log. Do not create a separate AuditLog list — the data is the same and keeping it in one place makes reporting simpler.

**Add these columns to `Change Log`:**

| Column | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Agent` | Lookup → Agents | No | Links audit entry to an agent record |
| `Field changed` | Single line | No | Name of the field that was changed |
| `Old value` | Multi-line | No | Value before the change |
| `New value` | Multi-line | No | Value after the change |
| `Changed by email` | Single line | No | User().Email at time of change |
| `Change type` | Choice | No | Values: `Field update`, `Gate decision`, `Stage transition`, `Review event`, `Sync event` |
| `Change timestamp` | Date/Time | No | Now() at time of change |

> The existing `Change Log` columns (`Title`, `Changed by`, etc.) are preserved. The additions are additive only.

---

### 2.3 Extend Existing List: `Agents`

Add these fields to the existing Agents list:

| Column | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Submitted By` | Person | No | — | Auto-set to User() on intake creation; separate from Owner |
| `Governance Review Required` | Yes/No | No | No | Admin sets to Yes for existing agents needing governance review |

> `Submitted By` is set on Patch at intake creation and is read-only after that (enforced in app, not SharePoint permissions).

---

## 3. RBAC Design

### 3.1 Permission Matrix

Rows = roles. Columns = app capabilities. ✓ = can do. ✗ = cannot. (R) = read-only.

| Capability | Admin | GateApprover | AIS_Reviewer | Evaluator | Developer | ReadOnly |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| View all screens | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Create new agent (intake) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ |
| Edit agent core fields (name, owner, summary) | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
| Edit template sections (instructions, topics, user story) | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
| Set evaluation outcome + feasibility score | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ |
| Set AIS review outcome + notes | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| Validate knowledge source sensitivity | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| Approve DoR gate | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| Approve DoD gate | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| Approve Production Readiness gate | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| Add/edit test questions | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
| Record test results | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
| Add/edit knowledge sources | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
| Add actions | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ |
| Close/complete actions | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ |
| Manage Agent Roles list | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| Set Governance Review Required flag | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| View audit/change log | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Trigger manual ADO sync refresh | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ |

---

### 3.2 Power FX Implementation

#### App.OnStart — role resolution

Add this to `App.OnStart` (after existing ClearCollect calls):

```powerfx
// RBAC: Load current user role from Agent Roles list
ClearCollect(
    colCurrentUserRole,
    Filter(
        'Agent Roles',
        Lower(UserEmail) = Lower(User().Email),
        IsActive = true
    )
);

// Set role globals — used by every screen to show/hide/enable controls
Set(gvUserRole,
    If(
        CountRows(colCurrentUserRole) > 0,
        First(colCurrentUserRole).Role,
        "ReadOnly"
    )
);

// Convenience booleans for clean control expressions
Set(gvIsAdmin,        gvUserRole = "Admin");
Set(gvIsGateApprover, gvUserRole in ["Admin", "GateApprover"]);
Set(gvIsAISReviewer,  gvUserRole in ["Admin", "AIS_Reviewer"]);
Set(gvIsEvaluator,    gvUserRole in ["Admin", "Evaluator"]);
Set(gvIsDeveloper,    gvUserRole in ["Admin", "Developer", "GateApprover"]);
Set(gvCanCreate,      gvUserRole <> "ReadOnly");
```

> Do NOT call `Filter('Agent Roles', ...)` on every screen navigation. The `colCurrentUserRole` collection is loaded once at startup. This avoids delegation issues and keeps navigation fast.

#### Role-gating controls (pattern — apply per screen)

**Disable a field for non-permitted roles:**
```powerfx
// Example: Evaluation outcome dropdown
EvaluationOutcomeDropdown.DisplayMode = 
    If(gvIsEvaluator, DisplayMode.Edit, DisplayMode.View)
```

**Hide a button for non-permitted roles:**
```powerfx
// Example: Approve DoR gate button
ApproveDORButton.Visible = gvIsGateApprover
```

**Show a read-only label instead of an editable control:**
```powerfx
// Example: AIS review notes text input
AISNotesInput.Visible = gvIsAISReviewer
AISNotesLabel.Visible = !gvIsAISReviewer
AISNotesLabel.Text = gvSelectedAgent.'AIS review notes'
```

---

### 3.3 Screen-by-Screen Role Changes

Apply the following role gates to existing screens. Do not rebuild screens — only modify `DisplayMode`, `Visible`, and `Enabled` on existing controls.

#### Intake Screen

| Control | Change |
|---|---|
| Submit button | `Visible = gvCanCreate` |
| On `Patch()` for new agent creation | Add `{'Submitted By': {Id: User().Id, DisplayName: User().FullName, Email: User().Email}, 'Governance Review Required': false}` to the Patch record |

#### Agent Detail — Summary Tab

| Control | Change |
|---|---|
| Agent name, owner, department fields | `DisplayMode = If(gvIsDeveloper, DisplayMode.Edit, DisplayMode.View)` |
| Governance Review Required toggle | `Visible = gvIsAdmin` |

#### Agent Detail — Gate Review Tab

| Control | Change |
|---|---|
| Evaluation outcome dropdown + feasibility score | `DisplayMode = If(gvIsEvaluator, DisplayMode.Edit, DisplayMode.View)` |
| AIS review outcome + AIS notes | `DisplayMode = If(gvIsAISReviewer, DisplayMode.Edit, DisplayMode.View)` |
| DoR approve button | `Visible = gvIsGateApprover` |

## 4. Audit Log Design

### 4.1 What Gets Audited

Every write to a governance-sensitive field must produce a `Change Log` entry. "Governance-sensitive" means the field affects a gate decision, a review outcome, or a lifecycle stage.

| Field / Action | Change Type |
|---|---|
| `Evaluation outcome` | `Field update` |
| `Feasibility score` | `Field update` |
| `AIS review outcome` | `Field update` |
| `AIS review notes` | `Field update` |
| `DoR gate status` | `Gate decision` |
| `DoD gate status` | `Gate decision` |
| `Production readiness gate status` | `Gate decision` |
| `Lifecycle status` (stage transition) | `Stage transition` |
| `Knowledge source Sensitivity` field change | `Field update` |
| ADO sync run | `Sync event` |

Non-audited writes (template content, test question creation, action creation) do not require audit entries. The SharePoint version history covers these.

---

### 4.2 Power FX Audit Write Pattern

Use this exact pattern. Capture old value BEFORE the Patch, write audit entry AFTER.

```powerfx
// Pattern: audit a field change
// Step 1 — capture old value before patch
Set(gvAuditOld, gvSelectedAgent.'Evaluation outcome');

// Step 2 — patch the field
Patch(
    Agents,
    gvSelectedAgent,
    {'Evaluation outcome': ddEvaluationOutcome.Selected.Value}
);

// Step 3 — write audit entry
Patch(
    'Change Log',
    Defaults('Change Log'),
    {
        Title: "Evaluation outcome updated — " & gvSelectedAgent.Title,
        Agent: {Id: gvSelectedAgent.ID},
        'Field changed': "Evaluation outcome",
        'Old value': gvAuditOld,
        'New value': ddEvaluationOutcome.Selected.Value,
        'Changed by': User().FullName,
        'Changed by email': User().Email,
        'Change type': "Field update",
        'Change timestamp': Now()
    }
);
```

**Gate decision variant (DoR approve):**

```powerfx
// Step 1 — capture current gate status
Set(gvAuditOld, gvSelectedAgent.'DoR gate status');

// Step 2 — patch gate status
Patch(
    Agents,
    gvSelectedAgent,
    {
        'DoR gate status': "Approved",
        'DoR approver': {Id: User().Id, DisplayName: User().FullName, Email: User().Email},
        'DoR date': Today()
    }
);

// Step 3 — write audit entry
Patch(
    'Change Log',
    Defaults('Change Log'),
    {
        Title: "DoR gate approved — " & gvSelectedAgent.Title,
        Agent: {Id: gvSelectedAgent.ID},
        'Field changed': "DoR gate status",
        'Old value': gvAuditOld,
        'New value': "Approved",
        'Changed by': User().FullName,
        'Changed by email': User().Email,
        'Change type': "Gate decision",
        'Change timestamp': Now()
    }
);

// Step 4 — refresh selected agent record
Set(gvSelectedAgent, LookupValue(Agents, Agents.ID = gvSelectedAgent.ID));
```

---

│                                                                 │

│                    Agent: HR Chatbot                            │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Gallery formula:**

        Descending
    )
```

> Note: This filter on the Change Log is on Lookup and Choice fields — both are not fully delegable. Pre-load last 500 entries into a collection at screen navigate if delegation warnings appear.

---

## 5. ADO Sync Flow Specification

### 5.1 Overview

A Power Automate flow reads Azure DevOps work item state for each agent that has an `ADO Work Item ID` populated, and writes back 13 delivery-state fields into the SharePoint `Agents` list. The flow also writes a summary entry to the `Sync Audit` list.

The existing `Sync Audit` list is already present in the data model — use it.

---

### 5.2 Flow Triggers

Two triggers on the same flow:

| Trigger | Config |
|---|---|
| **Recurrence** | Every 60 minutes |
| **HTTP (manual)** | PowerApp calls this via `PowerAutomateFlow.Run()` when user taps "Refresh ADO" button |

Use a single flow with a **When an HTTP request is received** trigger plus a Recurrence trigger in parallel branches (or duplicate the flow — simpler for maintenance).

**Recommended: two separate flows** — one scheduled, one HTTP-triggered from the app. They share the same core action steps (extract as a child flow via scope + compose, or just duplicate the steps — at this scale, duplication is acceptable).

---

### 5.3 Authentication

Use a **Service Account** connection (or managed identity if Power Automate Premium is available) with:
- SharePoint connector: delegated, service account with edit access to Agents list and Sync Audit list
- Azure DevOps connector (built-in): Personal Access Token or OAuth — PAT recommended for simplicity

ADO PAT scopes required: `Work Items (Read)`

---

### 5.4 Flow Steps — Core Sync Logic

```
1. INITIALIZE VARIABLES
   - varSuccessCount (Integer, 0)
   - varErrorCount (Integer, 0)
   - varRunTimestamp (String, utcNow())
   - varErrors (Array, [])

2. GET AGENTS WITH ADO LINK
   Action: SharePoint — Get items
   Site: [SharePoint site URL]
   List: Agents
   Filter query: ADOWorkItemId ne ''
   Top: 500
   (This returns all agents that have an ADO work item linked)

3. APPLY TO EACH (item from step 2)

   3a. TRY — HTTP request to ADO
       Method: GET
       URI: https://dev.azure.com/Ofgem-DDaT/Copilot%20Studio%20Agents/_apis/wit/workitems/@{items('Apply_to_each')?['ADOWorkItemId']}?$expand=all&api-version=7.0
       Authentication: Basic (PAT)
       
   3b. CONDITION — Did HTTP call succeed? (Status code = 200)
   
   IF YES:
       3c. PARSE JSON — parse the ADO response body
           Schema: { id, fields: { System.State, System.AssignedTo, System.AreaPath, 
                     System.IterationPath, Microsoft.VSTS.Build.SourceBranch,
                     System.TeamProject, System.ChangedDate } }
       
       3d. UPDATE SharePoint item (Agents list)
           Item ID: @{items('Apply_to_each')?['ID']}
           Fields to update:
           - ADODeliveryState: @{body('Parse_ADO_JSON')?['fields']?['System.State']}
           - ADOAssignedTo: @{body('Parse_ADO_JSON')?['fields']?['System.AssignedTo']?['displayName']}
           - ADOAreaPath: @{body('Parse_ADO_JSON')?['fields']?['System.AreaPath']}
           - ADOIterationPath: @{body('Parse_ADO_JSON')?['fields']?['System.IterationPath']}
           - ADOBuildBranch: @{body('Parse_ADO_JSON')?['fields']?['Microsoft.VSTS.Build.SourceBranch']}
           - ADOLastSyncedAt: @{varRunTimestamp}
           - ADOWorkItemUrl: https://dev.azure.com/Ofgem-DDaT/Copilot%20Studio%20Agents/_workitems/edit/@{items('Apply_to_each')?['ADOWorkItemId']}
       
       3e. INCREMENT varSuccessCount: add(variables('varSuccessCount'), 1)
   
   IF NO (HTTP failed):
       3f. UPDATE SharePoint item — write error signal
           - ADOLastSyncedAt: @{varRunTimestamp}
           - ADODeliveryState: "Sync error"
       
       3g. APPEND TO varErrors:
           { "agentId": "@{items('Apply_to_each')?['ID']}", 
             "title": "@{items('Apply_to_each')?['Title']}",
             "statusCode": "@{outputs('HTTP_ADO_Call')?['statusCode']}" }
       
       3h. INCREMENT varErrorCount: add(variables('varErrorCount'), 1)

4. WRITE SYNC AUDIT ENTRY
   Action: SharePoint — Create item
   List: Sync Audit
   Fields:
   - Title: "ADO Sync — @{varRunTimestamp}"
   - Run timestamp: @{varRunTimestamp}
   - Agents processed: @{length(body('Get_agents_with_ADO_link')?['value'])}
   - Success count: @{variables('varSuccessCount')}
   - Error count: @{variables('varErrorCount')}
   - Error detail: @{string(variables('varErrors'))}
   - Triggered by: Scheduled (or "Manual — [user]" if HTTP trigger)
```

---

### 5.5 PowerApp "Refresh ADO" Button

Add to the Agent Detail screen — Delivery tab, next to the ADO link fields. Visible to all roles except ReadOnly.

```powerfx
// Button: OnSelect
Set(gvADOSyncRunning, true);

// Call the HTTP-triggered flow
PowerAutomateFlow_ADOSync.Run(
    gvSelectedAgent.ID,          // pass the single agent ID for targeted sync
    User().Email                  // for audit trail
);

// Refresh the agent record after sync
Set(
    gvSelectedAgent,
    LookupValue(Agents, Agents.ID = gvSelectedAgent.ID)
);

Set(gvADOSyncRunning, false);
Notify("ADO delivery state refreshed", NotificationType.Success);
```

> The HTTP-triggered flow variant should accept `agentId` as input and only sync that one record (not all agents). This keeps the on-demand refresh fast. The scheduled flow syncs all.

---

| Column | Type | New? |

| `Submitted By` | Person | **New** |

## 7. Implementation Sequence for Codex

Execute in this order. Each step is independently testable before moving to the next.

### Step 1 — Data model (SharePoint, no app changes)

1. Create `Agent Roles` list with columns per section 2.1
2. Add columns to `Change Log` per section 2.2
3. Add `Submitted By` (Person) and `Governance Review Required` (Yes/No) to `Agents` list
4. Set SharePoint list permissions on `Agent Roles`: Admin users = Full Control; all others = Read
5. Seed at least one Admin role entry for the test user email
6. **Test:** Confirm all lists and columns exist with correct types. Run `scripts/sharepoint-validation` if available.

### Step 2 — RBAC in app (App.OnStart + all screens)

1. Add RBAC block to `App.OnStart` per section 3.2
2. Add `gvUserRole` display to Admin screen for debug (remove before release)
3. Apply permission matrix controls to each screen per section 3.3
4. Add Role Management UI to Admin screen per section 3.4
5. **Test:** Log in as three different test accounts (Admin / Developer / ReadOnly). Confirm each sees the correct controls. Confirm ReadOnly cannot edit anything.

### Step 3 — Audit log (Change Log writes)

1. Add audit write Patch() calls to all governance field saves per section 4.2
   - Priority order: Gate decisions first, then evaluation/AIS outcomes, then sensitivity flags
2. Add Audit Trail section to Reports screen per section 4.3
3. **Test:** Approve a DoR gate. Confirm Change Log contains the entry with correct Old/New values and timestamp.

### Step 4 — Intake screen: Submitted By capture

1. On intake Patch(), add `Submitted By` = User() and `Governance Review Required` = false
2. Display `Submitted By` on the agent detail Summary tab (read-only label)
3. Add `Governance Review Required` toggle on Summary tab, visible only when `gvIsAdmin = true`
4. On Home/Dashboard: add a "Governance review needed" banner/chip visible when agent flag is true
5. **Test:** Create a test agent via intake. Confirm `Submitted By` is set and is different from `Owner` if edited.

### Step 5 — ADO sync flow

1. Build the scheduled flow per section 5.4
2. Build the HTTP-triggered single-agent variant
3. Add "Refresh ADO" button to Agent Detail Delivery tab per section 5.5
4. Test against a known ADO work item ID in the `Copilot Studio Agents` project
5. Confirm `Sync Audit` list receives a run entry after each execution
6. **Test:** Trigger manual refresh from app. Confirm ADODeliveryState updates and Sync Audit entry appears.

### Step 6 — Validation pass

1. Run through permission matrix end-to-end with three user accounts
2. Confirm every audit-required field change creates a Change Log entry
3. Confirm ADO sync populates all 13 delivery fields when ADO work item exists
4. Confirm `Submitted By` differs from `Owner` on at least one test agent
5. PAC pack and unpack the final `.msapp` — confirm clean import

---

## 8. Test Criteria

| ID | Criterion | How to verify |
|---|---|---|
| TC-01 | ReadOnly user cannot edit any field on any screen | Log in as ReadOnly user; all editable controls show in View mode |
| TC-02 | Developer user can edit template but not evaluation outcome | Log in as Developer; AIS/eval fields in View mode, template fields in Edit mode |
| TC-03 | AIS Reviewer can set AIS outcome but not approve DoR gate | Log in as AIS_Reviewer; AIS fields editable, DoR button hidden |
| TC-04 | GateApprover can approve all three gates | Log in as GateApprover; all three gate approve buttons visible |
| TC-05 | Approving DoR gate creates Change Log entry | Approve DoR; query Change Log for Change type = "Gate decision" |
| TC-06 | Old value is captured correctly in audit | Change AIS outcome from A to B; Change Log Old value = A |
| TC-07 | Intake form sets Submitted By to current user | Create agent; confirm `Submitted By` = test user |
| TC-08 | Submitted By is not changed when Owner is edited | Edit Owner on Summary tab; confirm Submitted By unchanged |
| TC-09 | ADO sync populates ADODeliveryState from live ADO item | Set known ADO ID; trigger sync; confirm field updates |
| TC-10 | ADO sync error writes "Sync error" to ADODeliveryState | Set invalid ADO ID; trigger sync; confirm error state |
| TC-11 | Sync Audit list receives entry after each sync run | Trigger sync; confirm new row with success/error counts |
| TC-12 | Admin screen Role Management shows current roles | Log in as Admin; confirm gallery shows Agent Roles list |
| TC-13 | Non-admin cannot see Role Management section | Log in as Developer; confirm section invisible |
| TC-14 | Governance Review Required flag visible only to Admin | Log in as Developer on Summary tab; flag toggle invisible |
| TC-15 | Reports Audit Trail shows last 500 Change Log entries sorted descending | Navigate to Reports; confirm entries visible newest-first |
| TC-16 | PAC pack/unpack produces clean import | Run PAC; confirm 0 errors, 0 import warnings |

---

## 9. Dropped / Deferred Items

| Item | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Gate enforcement (R1) | Post-pilot | Not needed for pilot per Product Owner |
| Kanban board (R5) | Dropped v1 | Nice-to-have, too complex for Canvas |

| AAD security group integration | Enhancement path | AgentRoles list approach is simpler and doesn't need AAD admin; revisit at ~200 users |
| Multi-role per user | Deferred | Single role per user is sufficient now; add if roles prove too coarse |

## Power FX: App.OnStart RBAC Block

```powerfx
ClearCollect(
    colCurrentUserRole,
    Filter('Agent Roles', Lower(UserEmail) = Lower(User().Email), IsActive = true)
);
Set(gvUserRole,
    If(CountRows(colCurrentUserRole) > 0, First(colCurrentUserRole).Role, "ReadOnly")
);
Set(gvIsAdmin,        gvUserRole = "Admin");
Set(gvIsGateApprover, gvUserRole in ["Admin", "GateApprover"]);
Set(gvIsAISReviewer,  gvUserRole in ["Admin", "AIS_Reviewer"]);
Set(gvIsEvaluator,    gvUserRole in ["Admin", "Evaluator"]);
Set(gvIsDeveloper,    gvUserRole in ["Admin", "Developer", "GateApprover"]);
Set(gvCanCreate,      gvUserRole <> "ReadOnly");

## Power FX: Audit Write Pattern

```powerfx
// Capture old value BEFORE patch
Set(gvAuditOld, gvSelectedAgent.'Evaluation outcome');

// Patch the field
Patch(Agents, gvSelectedAgent, {'Evaluation outcome': ddEvaluationOutcome.Selected.Value});

// Write audit entry AFTER patch

    Title: "Evaluation outcome updated — " & gvSelectedAgent.Title,

    'Field changed': "Evaluation outcome",
    'Old value': gvAuditOld,
    'New value': ddEvaluationOutcome.Selected.Value,
    'Changed by': User().FullName,
    'Changed by email': User().Email,

## ADO Sync Flow

**Trigger:** Recurrence every 60 min + HTTP trigger (PowerApp "Refresh ADO" button)

1. GET Agents list where ADOWorkItemId is not blank
2. For each agent:

         _apis/wit/workitems/{ADOWorkItemId}?$expand=all&api-version=7.0
   b. If 200: update Agents item with ADO fields
   c. If error: set ADODeliveryState = "Sync error"
3. Write summary row to Sync Audit list
```

**13 fields written back to Agents list:**
`ADODeliveryState` · `ADOAssignedTo` · `ADOAreaPath` · `ADOIterationPath` · `ADOBuildBranch` · `ADOLastSyncedAt` · `ADOWorkItemUrl` · (+ 6 others in full spec)

5. **Step 5** — ADO sync flow: Build scheduled flow + HTTP-triggered single-agent variant + Refresh ADO button
6. **Step 6** — Validation: Permission matrix end-to-end test, audit trail test, ADO sync test, PAC pack/unpack
